description: Pineapple Bun, or Bo Lo Bao, is a beloved Hong Kong bakery classic featuring a soft, sweet bread topped with a crispy, crumbly, cookie-like crust. Despite its name, it contains no pineapple, instead deriving its name from the pineapple-like appearance of its golden, checkered topping. This delightful bun offers a perfect balance of textures and flavors, making it a popular treat for breakfast or afternoon tea.

instructions.title: Prepare the Bun Dough
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine 250g all-purpose flour, 30g granulated sugar, 3g instant dry yeast, and 2g salt. Gradually add 120ml warm milk and 1 beaten egg. Mix until a shaggy dough forms. Turn onto a lightly floured surface and knead for 8-10 minutes until smooth and elastic. Incorporate 25g softened unsalted butter and knead for another 5 minutes until the butter is fully absorbed and the dough is very smooth. Place the dough in a greased bowl, cover with plastic wrap, and let it rise in a warm place for 60-90 minutes, or until doubled in size.

instructions.title: Make the Pineapple Topping
instructions.text: While the dough is rising, prepare the topping. In a separate bowl, combine 100g all-purpose flour, 50g granulated sugar, 10g powdered milk, and 2g baking powder. Add 60g cold, diced unsalted butter and rub it into the dry ingredients using your fingertips until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Add 1 large egg yolk and mix until a soft dough forms. Do not overmix. Wrap the topping dough in plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes to firm up.

instructions.title: Shape the Buns
instructions.text: Once the bun dough has doubled, gently punch it down to release air. Divide the dough into 8 equal pieces, about 50-60g each. Roll each piece into a smooth ball. Place the dough balls on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, leaving space between them. For the topping, divide the chilled topping dough into 8 equal pieces. Flatten each piece into a thin, round disc, about 3-4 inches in diameter. You can use plastic wrap on top and bottom to make rolling easier and prevent sticking.

instructions.title: Apply Topping and Second Rise
instructions.text: Carefully place one topping disc over each bun dough ball, gently pressing down to adhere. The topping should cover most of the bun's surface, leaving a small border of the bun dough visible at the bottom. Use a dull knife or a pastry scraper to gently score a crosshatch pattern onto the surface of each topping, mimicking the look of a pineapple. Cover the buns loosely with plastic wrap or a clean kitchen towel and let them rise again in a warm place for 30-45 minutes, or until visibly puffy.

instructions.title: Bake the Pineapple Buns
instructions.text: Preheat your oven to 180°C (350°F). Just before baking, gently brush the exposed bun dough (not the topping) with the egg wash (1 beaten egg mixed with 1 tbsp water). This helps achieve a golden color. Bake the pineapple buns for 15-20 minutes, or until the topping is golden brown and crispy and the buns are cooked through. Keep an eye on them to prevent over-browning.

instructions.title: Cool and Serve
instructions.text: Once baked, remove the pineapple buns from the oven and transfer them to a wire rack to cool slightly. Pineapple buns are best enjoyed warm, when the topping is still crispy and the bun is soft and fragrant. You can slice them horizontally and insert a thick slice of cold butter for an extra decadent experience, a popular way to enjoy them in Hong Kong bakeries.

tips: For an extra crispy topping, ensure your butter for the topping is very cold. You can even grate it into the flour mixture.
Do not overmix the topping dough; overworking gluten will result in a tough, rather than crumbly, texture.
Pineapple buns are best eaten fresh and warm. If storing, reheat in a toaster oven for a few minutes to restore crispness.
article:
Unlock the secrets to one of Hong Kong's most beloved bakery treats: the Pineapple Bun, or Bo Lo Bao. This iconic pastry, a staple in dim sum restaurants and bakeries across the globe, offers a delightful contrast of textures and flavors. With its soft, slightly sweet bread base and a crisp, sugary, cookie-like crust, it's a culinary experience that transports you straight to the bustling streets of a traditional Chinese bakery. While it contains no pineapple, its name comes from the distinctive criss-cross pattern on its golden-brown topping, which resembles the skin of a pineapple. Making authentic Bo Lo Bao at home might seem daunting, but with this comprehensive guide, you'll be well on your way to baking these irresistible delights.

## What is Pineapple Bun (Bo Lo Bao)?

The Pineapple Bun, or Bo Lo Bao (菠蘿包), is a sweet bun originating from Hong Kong, deeply ingrained in Cantonese culinary culture. Despite its name, it contains no pineapple; rather, the "pineapple" refers to the signature crumbly, sugary crust baked on top, which browns and cracks to resemble a pineapple's rough exterior. The bun itself is a soft, fluffy, slightly sweet yeast bread, similar to a brioche or milk bread. This combination of a pillowy interior and a crunchy, sweet exterior is what makes the Pineapple Bun so incredibly popular. It’s often enjoyed for breakfast, a snack, or alongside a cup of milk tea, sometimes served warm with a slice of butter tucked inside, creating the famous "Bo Lo Yau" (菠蘿油). Its unique texture and comforting sweetness have made it a quintessential item in Chinese bakeries worldwide.

## Ingredients for Authentic Pineapple Buns

Crafting authentic Pineapple Buns requires two main components: the soft bread dough and the characteristic crumbly topping. Each plays a crucial role in achieving the perfect texture and flavor.

For the Soft Bread Dough:
*   All-purpose flour: Provides the structure for the bun.
*   Granulated sugar: Adds sweetness and helps with browning.
*   Active dry yeast: The leavening agent that makes the bread rise and become fluffy.
*   Milk: Adds richness and moisture to the dough.
*   Egg: Contributes to the richness, color, and tenderness of the bun.
*   Unsalted butter: Enhances flavor, texture, and tenderness.
*   Salt: Balances the sweetness and strengthens the gluten structure.

For the Pineapple Topping:
*   All-purpose flour: Forms the base of the crumbly topping.
*   Granulated sugar: Provides sweetness and helps create the crisp texture.
*   Unsalted butter: Chilled and cubed, it's essential for creating the crumbly, shortbread-like texture.
*   Egg yolk: Adds richness, color, and acts as a binder.
*   Baking powder: Helps the topping become light and crisp.
*   Milk powder (optional): Enhances flavor and richness, often used in professional bakeries.

An egg wash (beaten egg) will also be needed for brushing the topping before baking, giving the Pineapple Bun its beautiful golden sheen.

## Step-by-Step Pineapple Bun Recipe

Making homemade Pineapple Buns is a rewarding process. Here’s a simplified guide to bring these bakery favorites to your kitchen.

1.  Prepare the Dough: In a stand mixer, combine flour, sugar, yeast, and salt. Add warm milk, egg, and melted butter. Knead on low speed until a shaggy dough forms, then increase speed and knead for 8-10 minutes until the dough is smooth, elastic, and passes the windowpane test.
2.  First Proof: Place the dough in a lightly oiled bowl, cover with plastic wrap, and let it rise in a warm place for 1-1.5 hours, or until doubled in size.
3.  Prepare the Topping: While the dough proofs, combine flour, sugar, baking powder, and milk powder (if using) in a bowl. Cut in the cold, cubed butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Add the egg yolk and mix until a soft dough forms. Do not overmix. Wrap the topping dough in plastic and chill in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes.
4.  Shape the Buns: Once the dough has doubled, punch it down gently to release air. Divide the dough into 8-10 equal pieces (about 60-70g each). Roll each piece into a smooth ball and place them on a parchment-lined baking sheet, spaced apart.
5.  Shape the Topping: Divide the chilled topping dough into the same number of pieces as the bread dough. On a lightly floured surface or between two sheets of parchment paper, roll out each piece of topping dough into a thin disc, large enough to cover about two-thirds of a bun.
6.  Assemble: Carefully place a topping disc over each shaped bread bun. Gently press the topping down, making sure it adheres to the bun. Using a knife or dough scraper, lightly score a criss-cross pattern on the topping – this creates the "pineapple" effect.
7.  Second Proof: Cover the shaped buns loosely with plastic wrap and let them rise again in a warm place for 30-45 minutes, or until visibly puffy.
8.  Bake: Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C). Just before baking, lightly brush the topping with egg wash. Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until the buns are golden brown and the topping is crisp.
9.  Cool: Transfer the baked Pineapple Buns to a wire rack to cool slightly before serving.

## Tips for Perfect Bo Lo Bao

Achieving that perfect bakery-quality Bo Lo Bao at home is within reach with a few key tips:

*   **Don't Rush Proofing:** Proper proofing is crucial for a fluffy bun. Allow the dough ample time to rise in a warm, draft-free environment. Under-proofed dough results in dense buns, while over-proofed dough can lead to a yeasty flavor and collapse.
*   **Cold Topping is Key:** Ensure your topping dough is well-chilled before rolling and applying. This prevents it from melting too quickly in the oven, allowing it to maintain its shape and crispness. If it gets too warm, chill it again.
*   **Handle Topping Gently:** The topping is delicate. Roll it out carefully and place it gently over the buns. Don't press too hard, as this can flatten the bun and prevent it from rising properly.
*   **Scoring Technique:** Use a sharp knife or dough scraper to score the criss-cross pattern. Don't cut too deep into the bread dough, just enough to create the distinct pineapple texture on the topping.
*   **Egg Wash for Shine:** A light brush of egg wash (one beaten egg) on the topping before baking gives the Pineapple Bun its characteristic golden-brown, glossy finish.
*   **Oven Temperature:** Ensure your oven is preheated to the correct temperature. An oven thermometer can be very helpful here. Baking at the right temperature ensures even cooking and browning of both the bun and the topping.

## Serving Your Homemade Pineapple Buns

One of the greatest joys of baking homemade Pineapple Buns is enjoying them fresh from the oven. The aroma alone is enough to make mouths water! Traditionally, Bo Lo Bao is best served warm, allowing the bread to remain soft and the topping to retain its crispness.

Many people enjoy their Pineapple Buns plain, savoring the simple yet perfect combination of sweet crust and fluffy bread. However, a popular way to elevate this classic is to slice it horizontally and insert a thick slab of cold, unsalted butter (this is known as Bo Lo Yau, or "Pineapple Butter Bun"). The cold butter slowly melts into the warm bun, creating a luxurious, savory-sweet experience that is utterly addictive. This is a must-try for any true fan.

Pair your Pineapple Bun with a classic Hong Kong-style milk tea, a cup of strong coffee, or simply a glass of milk for a comforting breakfast or afternoon tea snack. They are also a fantastic addition to any dim sum spread.

## Pineapple Bun Variations & Substitutions

While the classic Pineapple Bun is a masterpiece in itself, there are several delicious variations and substitutions you can explore to customize this beloved pastry.

*   **Filled Pineapple Buns:** Many bakeries offer filled versions. Common fillings include:
    *   **Custard Cream:** A smooth, sweet egg custard adds a delightful creamy element.
    *   **Char Siu (BBQ Pork):** For a savory twist, a sweet and savory BBQ pork filling creates a delicious contrast with the sweet topping.
    *   **Red Bean Paste:** A traditional sweet bean paste offers a rich, earthy sweetness.
    *   **Coconut Filling:** Shredded coconut mixed with sugar and butter provides a tropical, chewy center.
*   **Topping Variations:**
    *   **Sesame Seeds:** A sprinkle of white sesame seeds on the topping before baking adds a nutty flavor and visual appeal.
    *   **Less Sweet Topping:** For those who prefer less sugar, you can slightly reduce the sugar content in the topping recipe.
*   **Dietary Adjustments:**
    *   **Vegan Options:** Substitute dairy milk with plant-based milk, and use a flax egg or commercial egg replacer for the egg in the dough. For the topping, use a vegan butter substitute and omit the egg yolk, potentially adjusting with a tiny bit of plant milk to bring the dough together.
    *   **Gluten-Free:** While challenging due to the importance of gluten for the bun's texture, some specialized gluten-free flour blends may work, though the final texture will differ.

Experimenting with these variations can lead to new favorite ways to enjoy your homemade Pineapple Bun, making this classic even more versatile and personal.

Baking your own Pineapple Buns is a delightful culinary journey that brings the authentic taste of Chinese bakeries right into your home. With a little patience and these detailed instructions, you’ll soon be enjoying these iconic treats, fresh and perfectly baked.
